message.content:
The famous scene where Del Boy falls through the bar is from the episode **"Yuppy Love"**, which was the first episode of **Series 6** of *Only Fools and Horses*. It originally aired on **January 8, 1989** on BBC1.

In this iconic scene, Del Boy (played by Sir David Jason) and Trigger (played by Roger Lloyd Pack) are in a trendy wine bar trying to impress two women. Del tells Trigger to "play it nice and cool, son, nice and cool," but when he goes to lean on the bar, he doesn't realize the barman has lifted the counter hatch — and he falls straight through. Trigger then looks around wondering where Del has gone.

This scene is widely regarded as one of the greatest moments in British comedy history. It was voted the **funniest sitcom moment of all time** in a 2022 poll commissioned by UKTV Gold, and also topped a RadioTimes.com poll celebrating the show's 40th anniversary.

Interestingly, writer John Sullivan originally wanted Del to simply stumble and catch himself, based on a real-life incident he'd witnessed. However, David Jason — drawing on his experience in stage farces — insisted on falling all the way through, making the scene even funnier. Roger Lloyd Pack's presence as Trigger in the scene was also apparently unplanned; he happened to be at the BBC that day and was written into the scene at the last minute.
